# CompMD

> CompMD (Component Markdown) is CommonMark + GFM with components, containers, named slots, typed params, data, inputs and CSS-like layout. Files end in `.comp.md`. Every construct is one line, so a document stays readable in any plain Markdown renderer. This file is everything you need to write valid CompMD; the normative spec is compmd-spec-v1.md.

Read the ten rules first; most mistakes break one of them. Then use the sections as a reference. Syntax that looks like MDX, Markdoc, MDC, remark-directive, Pandoc or Jinja is usually wrong here: see "Habits from other formats".

## The ten rules

1. Block components use three colons and a **named closer**: `::: card {title="Setup"}` … `::: /card`. Never a bare `:::` closer, never four colons, always a space after the colons.
2. A leaf (a block with no body) uses two colons and a fallback in brackets: `:: chart[Weekly installs, up 18%] {rows=(md.data.installs)}`.
3. An inline component has one colon, a required fallback, and its params **directly** after `]`, with no space: `:badge[beta]{tone=info}`.
4. Named slots are `:: #name` lines inside a container. Default content comes first, before any slot line.
5. `{{path}}` inserts a value: dotted names only, no operators, no calls, no filters. Anything computed, even a single function such as `md.date(…)`, uses `:value[fallback]{of=(expression)}`: write `:value[October 21, 2026]{of=(md.date(md.doc.released, "long"))}`, never `{{md.date(md.doc.released, "long")}}`, which is shown as written.
6. Expressions go in parentheses in a param value, `name=(expr)`, and are CEL, not JavaScript: `size(x)`, not `x.length`; `==`, not `===`.
7. Everything CompMD provides is under `md.`: frontmatter is `md.doc.<key>`, data `md.data.<name>`, inputs `md.input.<name>`, slots `md.slot`, functions `md.currency(…)`. A bare `title` is not the frontmatter key.
8. Frontmatter: CompMD's own settings go under the `md:` key; every other key is the author's and is read as `md.doc.<key>`.
9. Put a blank line before and after every block component line (the opener, a leaf, a closer).
10. Every leaf and inline component gets a fallback written as a readable sentence or phrase: it is what plain renderers and failing renderers show.

## A document

````md
---
md:
  version: 1
  import:
    - from: "@acme/ui@1"
      names: [card, badge, chart]
title: Release notes
version: "1.4"
changes:
  - {text: "New renderer", pr: 412, breaking: false}
  - {text: "Config format 2", pr: 398, breaking: true}
---

# {{md.doc.title}} :badge[beta]{tone=info}

Version {{md.doc.version}} ships a new renderer.

::: card {title="Setup"}
Install with `cargo install rayplay`.

:: #footer
Takes about 2 minutes.
::: /card

## What changed

::: each {in=(md.doc.changes) as=c join=list}
- {{c.text}} ([#{{c.pr}}](https://github.com/acme/rayplay/pull/{{c.pr}}))
::: /each

::: if {when=(md.doc.changes.exists(c, c.breaking))}
Run `rayplay migrate` before upgrading.
:: #else
This release is backward compatible.
::: /if
````

## Frontmatter

YAML between `---` lines at the very top. Keys CompMD reads, all under `md:`:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | `1` (default), or a string such as `"1.1"` |
| `import` | components to import (see Imports) |
| `export` | components this document offers as a pack |
| `data` | data files or URLs, read as `md.data.<as>` |
| `inputs` | values the reader can change, read as `md.input.<name>` |
| `lang` | BCP 47 tag, default `en`; formatting functions follow it |
| `dir` | `ltr`, `rtl` or `auto` |
| `tz` | IANA time zone for `md.today()` |
| `syntax` | opt-in syntax: `[wiki-links]` enables `[[Page]]` |

- Any other key, at the top level, is the author's: `title: X` is `md.doc.title`. Don't put author keys under `md:` (W111) and don't put CompMD keys outside it.
- YAML 1.2 core schema: `no` and `yes` are strings, `2026-10-21` is a string, `1.10` is the number 1.1 (quote versions). No anchors, aliases, tags or duplicate keys (F033).
- `@compmd/core` (layout, `if`, `each`, `value`, input components) is always available; never list it under `import`.

## Block components

| Line | Form | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| container open | `::: name {params}` | `::: card {title="Setup" .wide}` |
| param continuation | `::: + params` (no braces) | `::: + md:grid-template-columns="2fr 1fr"` |
| container close | `::: /name` | `::: /card` |
| leaf | `:: name[fallback] {params}` | `:: chart[Sales by month] {rows=(md.data.sales)}` |
| named slot | `:: #name` | `:: #footer` |

- The closer repeats the opener's name and closes the innermost open container. Containers nest to any depth, also inside themselves.
- Indent component lines at most 3 spaces past their parent (4 makes a code block). Inside a list item, indent to the item's content; inside a quote, prefix `> ` as for any line.
- Open and close a container inside the same list item or quote.
- A slot name must be one the component declares. Each named slot at most once. Slot lines sit at the container's own level, never indented under a list item inside it.
- A component with no slots takes no body: write it as a leaf.
- Long param lists continue on `::: +` lines directly after the opener or leaf.
- `\::: card` and `\:badge[x]` are literal text.

## Inline components

`:name[fallback]{params}`, inside paragraphs, headings, list items and table cells.

- The fallback is required and is inline Markdown (it may contain other inline components).
- Params follow `]` with no space; `:badge[beta] {tone=info}` is a badge without params followed by text (W107).
- The `:` must start the line or follow white space or punctuation, so `10:30[x]` stays text.
- In a GFM table cell, write `|` as `\|`: `:badge[x]{show=(a \|\| b)}`.

## Params

| Written | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `title="Setup"` | string; may contain `{{path}}`; escape `\"` and `\\` |
| `icon=rocket` | bare value, typed by the signature (number, boolean, enum or string) |
| `count=3` | the number 3 if the param is a number, else the string `"3"` |
| `open` | boolean `true` |
| `rows=(md.data.sales)` | an expression; its type is the value's type |
| `tags=["a","b"]`, `meta={"id":1}` | JSON on one line |
| `.wide` | adds class `wide` (repeatable) |
| `#intro` | sets id `intro` |
| `md:gap=l` | `gap` from the `md` breakpoint (768 px) up |

- A bare value can't contain spaces, quotes, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{` or `}`. Quote it: `grid-template-columns="repeat(3, 1fr)"`, `title="{{md.doc.title}}"`, or use an expression: `title=(md.doc.title)`.
- `title=` with nothing after `=` is an error; write `title=""`.
- Each param once per invocation. `id` and `#name` are the same param.
- Every component accepts `class`, `id`, `lang` and `dir` without declaring them.
- Param names are kebab-case (`align-items`). Inside a definition's expressions and `{{ }}` they are written with `_` (`align_items`).
- `md:` in front of a param is a **breakpoint**, not the `md.` namespace. The breakpoints are `sm` (480 px), `md` (768 px) and `lg` (1024 px), mobile-first.

## Interpolation: `{{path}}`

| Path | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `md.doc.<key>` | everywhere: the author's frontmatter of the document it is written in |
| `md.version`, `md.lang`, `md.tz` | everywhere |
| `md.data.<name>` | everywhere |
| `md.input.<name>` | document bodies (not definition bodies) |
| `<param>` | inside a `compmd` definition body |
| `<as name>`, `md.loop.<field>` | inside `each` and template slots |
| `md.slot`, `md.slot.<name>` | inside a `compmd` definition body |

- Allowed in text, fallbacks, link and image URLs, quoted param strings and data `from` values. Not in code spans or code blocks (except in definition bodies), not in raw HTML: write `![logo]({{md.doc.logo}})`, not `<img src="{{md.doc.logo}}">`.
- A path is identifiers joined by `.`. No `{{ a + b }}`, `{{ x | upper }}`, `{{ rows[0] }}`, `{{#each}}` (W106 or F014). For anything computed use `:value[...]{of=(...)}`.
- Inserted as text, never parsed as Markdown. Numbers as `12.5`, booleans as `true`, `null` as nothing, a map with a `name` field as its name. A list or other map can't be inserted (F024): use `each`, or `:value[…]{of=(md.list(xs))}`.
- To write literal `{{` in prose, write `\{{` or use a code span.

## Expressions (CEL)

`name=(expr)`, on one line, in the CompMD profile of CEL (cel.dev).

- Variables: `md.doc`, `md.data`, `md.input`, `md.version`, `md.lang`, `md.tz`; inside definitions, the params; inside `each`, the `as` name and `md.loop`. Nothing else (no `window`, `Date`, `Math`, `env`).
- Operators: `== != < <= > >= && || ! + - * / % ?:`, `in`. Strings concatenate only with strings: `"Total: " + string(n)`.
- Functions: `size`, `has`, `int`, `double`, `string`, `timestamp`, `duration`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, and the strings extension `charAt indexOf lastIndexOf lowerAscii upperAscii replace split substring trim join`. No `matches`, no regular expressions.
- Macros on lists: `xs.filter(x, pred)`, `xs.map(x, expr)`, `xs.all(x, pred)`, `xs.exists(x, pred)`, `xs.exists_one(x, pred)`. On maps: `has(m.key)`.
- Numbers from data, frontmatter, params and inputs are doubles; literals, `size()` and `md.loop` fields are ints; mixing them is fine. `int / int` truncates: `double(size(rows)) / 2`. List indexes are ints: `rows[int(md.input.page)]`.
- Dates are ISO strings (`"2026-10-21"`) and compare with `<`, `>=`, `==`.
- Optional fields: guard with `has(r.note) ? r.note : ""`.

| CompMD function | Example | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `md.currency(n, code)` | `md.currency(price * 10, "USD")` | `"$120.00"` |
| `md.number(n, digits)` | `md.number(0.183 * 100, 0)` | `"18"` |
| `md.date(d, style)` | `md.date(md.doc.released, "long")` | `"October 21, 2026"`; styles `short medium long full` |
| `md.plural(n, one, other)` | `md.plural(n, "item", "items")` | the form for n; also `md.plural(n, {"one": …, "few": …, "other": …})` |
| `md.today()`, `md.now()` | | date string, timestamp |
| `md.dateOf(t)` | `md.dateOf(md.now())` | date of a timestamp |
| `md.addDays(d, n)` | `md.addDays(md.today(), -7)` | date |
| `md.daysBetween(a, b)` | `md.daysBetween(md.today(), md.doc.launch)` | int |
| `md.startOf(d, unit)` | `md.startOf(md.today(), "month")` | date; `"week"`, `"month"`, `"year"` |
| `md.sort(xs)`, `md.reverse(xs)` | `md.reverse(md.sort(md.doc.tags))` | list |
| `md.sortBy(xs, "field")` | `md.sortBy(md.data.sales, "amount")` | list, ascending, stable |
| `md.slice(xs, start, end)` | `md.slice(rows, 0, 5)` | list |
| `md.sum(xs)`, `md.min(xs)`, `md.max(xs)` | `md.sum(md.data.sales.map(s, s.amount))` | number (`min`/`max` of empty: null) |
| `md.unique(xs)` | `md.unique(md.data.sales.map(s, s.region))` | list |
| `md.groupBy(xs, "field")` | `md.groupBy(md.data.tasks, "status")` | map from value to elements |
| `md.list(xs)`, `md.list(xs, "or")` | `md.list(md.doc.authors)` | `"Ana, Kenji, and Priya"` |

List functions take a field name, not a function. To sort by something computed, `map` it into a field first: `md.sortBy(xs.map(x, {"x": x, "k": x.a * x.b}), "k")`.

## Control flow and computed text

`if`, `each` and `value` are ordinary `@compmd/core` components.

```md
::: if {when=(md.input.region != "all")}
Showing {{md.input.region}} only.
:: #else
Showing every region.
::: /if
```

`each`: `in` (required, a list), `as` (required, an identifier), `join` (`none` default, `list`, `inline`), `sep` and `last` for `inline`. Slots: default (once per item), `#before` (once, if any items), `#empty` (if none). `md.loop` has `index` (from 0), `number` (from 1), `count`, `first`, `last`.

```md
::: each {in=(md.data.team.filter(p, p.active)) as=p join=list}
- **{{p.name}}**, {{p.role}}

:: #before
## Team

:: #empty
Nobody yet.
::: /each

Built with:

::: each {in=(md.doc.stack) as=s join=inline sep=", " last=" and "}
[{{s.name}}]({{s.url}})
::: /each
```

- `join=list`: each iteration must be list items of one list type; they become one list. `join=inline`: each iteration exactly one paragraph. A single list item per iteration needs `join=list` (W103).
- `each` can't make table rows. A data table is a component (`:: table[…] {rows=(…)}`) from a pack.
- To repeat a component, put it inside `each`: `::: each {in=(md.data.team) as=p}` … `::: card {title="{{p.name}}"}` … `::: /card` … `::: /each`.

`value` prints a computed string; write the usual result as the fallback:

```md
The annual plan is :value[$120/year]{of=(md.currency(md.doc.price * 10, "USD") + "/year")}.
There are :value[3 open tasks]{of=(string(size(md.data.tasks)) + " open " + md.plural(size(md.data.tasks), "task", "tasks"))}.
```

`of` must be a string: wrap numbers in `string()` or a formatting function.

## Data

```yaml
md:
  data:
    - from: ./team.yaml          # YAML or JSON: its natural value
      as: team
    - from: ./sales.csv          # CSV/TSV: a list of maps by header
      as: sales
      schema: {date: date, region: string, amount: number}
    - from: ./orders.csv
      as: orders
      schema:
        unit_price: {from: "Unit price", type: number}   # rename non-identifier headers
    - from: https://api.example.com/status.json
      as: status
      cache: 1h
      fallback: ./status.json
    - from: host:tasks?status=open
      as: tasks
      schema: {title: string, due: date}
```

- Without `schema`, CSV values are strings. With it, cells are typed; `number?` allows empty cells.
- `from` may interpolate `md.input` and `md.doc` only, in the path or query: `./sales-{{md.input.year}}.csv`. The scheme and host of a URL are literal. Remote URLs are `https://` only.
- `host:` sources are data the processor provides; give them a `schema`.
- Relative paths resolve against the file they are written in.

## Inputs

```yaml
md:
  inputs:
    from: date = (md.addDays(md.today(), -30))
    region: all | eu | us = all
    min_amount: number = 0
    show_closed: boolean = false
    query: string = ""
```

```md
:: date-input[From: 30 days ago] {bind=from}
:: select-input[Region: all] {bind=region}
:: number-input[Minimum: 0] {bind=min_amount}
:: toggle-input[Show closed: no] {bind=show_closed}
:: text-input[Search] {bind=query}
```

- Every input has a default. Names are identifiers (snake_case).
- Input components: `date-input` (date), `number-input` (number), `text-input` (string), `select-input` (enum; members are the choices), `toggle-input` (boolean). `bind` names the input; write the default into the fallback.
- Inputs flow one way, into expressions: `rows=(md.data.sales.filter(s, s.date >= md.input.from))`. No events or scripts.

## Layout and styling

`@compmd/core` layout containers:

| Component | Lays out | Own params |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `box` | per `display` (`block`, `flex`, `grid`) | `display`, `flex-direction`, `gap`, `align-items`, `justify-content`, `flex-wrap`, `grid-template-columns`, `grid-template-rows`, `grid-template-areas` |
| `stack` | top to bottom | `gap`, `align-items` |
| `row` | side by side, wrapping | `gap`, `align-items`, `justify-content`, `flex-wrap` |
| `grid` | as many per row as fit (`min`), or an exact grid | `min`, `gap`, `align-items`, `grid-template-columns`, `grid-template-rows`, `grid-template-areas` |

Common params, on any container or leaf (they style its outer box):

- size: `width`, `height`, `min-width`, `max-width`, `aspect-ratio=16/9`
- spacing: `padding`, `padding-inline`, `padding-block`, `padding-inline-start` (and `-end`, `padding-block-start`, `-end`)
- look: `border` (`none subtle strong` or CSS), `border-radius` (`none s m l full` or a length), `background` (`none subtle strong accent` or a CSS color)
- placement: `grid-area`, `order` (`first last none`), `align-self`, `justify-self`, `inset-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`, `inset-block-start`, `inset-block-end`
- behavior: `scroll`, `fill`, `sticky=top|bottom`, `show=sm|md|lg`, `hide=sm|md|lg`

- Spaces (`gap`, padding): tokens `none`, `s`, `m`, `l`, or a length (`px rem em %`). Prefer tokens.
- Each top-level block in a layout container is one item. Wrap several blocks in `::: box` to make one item.
- `justify-content` takes `start center end between around`.
- Directions are logical only: `inline`/`block`, `start`/`end`. There is no `left`, `top`, `margin`, `color`, `font-size` or `style`. Unknown params are errors (F008); the vocabulary is closed, so raw CSS never passes.
- Breakpoints follow the width of the block's nearest box (the closest `box`, layout or component box around it; list items and quotes don't count), not the window and not the block's own width. Write the narrow layout first and override up: `::: grid {gap=s md:gap=l md:grid-template-columns="2fr 1fr"}`.
- A block with an `inset-*` is placed over its nearest box, which needs `height`, `aspect-ratio` or `fill` (W119).
- A box that holds blocks with breakpoints (`md:…`, `show`, `hide`) needs a `width` wherever its width would come from its content (W114): in a `row`; in a `stack` with `align-self` or `align-items` other than `stretch`, or `justify-self=center|end`; in a `grid` with `justify-self`; or positioned without both inline insets.

```md
::: grid {min=14rem gap=m}
::: card {title="Starter"}
For one person.
::: /card

::: card {title="Team"}
For up to ten.
::: /card
::: /grid

::: grid {grid-template-columns="12rem 1fr" grid-template-areas="'side main'" gap=m}
::: stack {grid-area=main}
Main content.
::: /stack

::: stack {grid-area=side}
Sidebar.
::: /stack
::: /grid
```

## Defining components

A definition is a fenced code block: language, then `component=<name>`, then optionally the box's params. It can be anywhere at document level; the name is visible to the whole document.

`compmd` definitions are written in CompMD: a YAML signature, a `---` line, then the body.

````md
```compmd component=callout {padding=m border=subtle border-radius=m background=subtle class=("callout-" + kind)}
params:
  kind: tip | warning = tip
  title: string?
slots: [default, footer]
---
# {{title}}

{{md.slot}}

{{md.slot.footer}}
```

::: callout {kind=warning title="Before you upgrade"}
Back up your config.

:: #footer
See the migration guide.
::: /callout
````

- Signature declarations: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `array`, `object`, `length`, `space`, `color`, `tracks`, `surface`, `border`, `radius`, `name`, an enum `a | b | c`, or `input<type>`. A `?` makes it optional; `= value` gives a default; no default and no `?` means required. Long form: `meta: {type: object, default: {a: 1}, doc: "…"}`.
- `slots: [default, footer]` lists slots; no `slots` key means no body. Template slot (rendered once per element): `slots: {default: {each: rows, as: as}}` with params `rows: array` and `as: name`.
- In the body: params by name (`{{title}}`, `(kind)`), `{{md.slot}}` and `{{md.slot.<name>}}` place slots, `md.doc` is the defining document's frontmatter, and there is no `md.input` (pass input values as params).
- Headings in a body are relative: `#` becomes one level below the heading the component is used under. Declare `headings: absolute` to keep written levels.
- **The box.** Each block use of a component is one box, like a custom element. The fence's params style it (common params, `class`, `id`, plus `box`'s own params such as `display=flex gap=s`); the caller's params override them per property. Don't wrap the body in `::: box` to style it: put the params on the fence.
- `display=contents` on the fence (and nothing else on it) gives the component no box: its blocks become the parent's items. Callers can't give it box params (W120).
- Inline use (`:name[...]{...}`) of a `compmd` component works when its body is one paragraph; it has no box.
- A definition whose body holds a code fence uses a longer outer fence (```` ```` ````) or `~~~`.
- Names: kebab-case. `if`, `each`, `value`, `box` and `md` are reserved. Param names that are CEL reserved words (`in`, `as`, `type`… see F013) can't be used in `compmd` definitions; name them `kind`, `items`, `variant`.
- No recursion (F019).

Host-language components (`jsx`, `tsx`, `svelte`, `js`, `ts`) are code that runs in a sandbox, with a `compmd` signature fence:

````md
```compmd component=chart signature
params:
  rows: array
  selected: input<enum>
```

```tsx component=chart runtime=react@19
export default function Chart({ rows, selected, compmd }) {
  return <svg role="img" aria-label={compmd.fallback.text}>…</svg>;
}
```
````

- React and Svelte 5: params are camelCase props, the default slot is `children`, named slots are props of their names, and `compmd` is `{slots, set, fallback, headingLevel, host}`. Plain `js`/`ts`: the default export is `mount(target, {params, slots, set, fallback, headingLevel, host})` returning `{update, destroy}`.
- A param typed `input<…>` is bound to an input by the caller (`selected=region`); the component calls `compmd.set("selected", "eu")` to change it. This is the only output a component has.
- The code has no network and sees only its params and slots. Use `fallback.text` as the accessible label of non-text content.
- A signature fence (`compmd component=<name> signature`) holds only the YAML signature, no `---`, no body, no param list.
- A component file (`./chart.jsx`) imported by path exports its default export, named after the file stem.

## Imports and exports

```yaml
md:
  import:
    - from: "@acme/ui@1"            # npm package, semver range; exact version for integrity
      names: [card, callout]
    - from: "@other/kit"
      names: [{name: card, as: promo-card}]
    - from: ./chart.jsx             # component file: one component, its default export
      names: [chart]
    - from: ./shared.comp.md        # another CompMD document's exports
      names: "*"
  export:
    pack: "@acme/release-kit"       # only to publish
    version: "1.2.0"
    names: [callout, {name: chart, as: trend-chart}]
```

- Packages are always scoped (`@scope/name`). Scoped names never appear in the body: import, then use the local name.
- Local definitions win over imports, imports over `@compmd/core`. Shadowing a core component is allowed but warned (W112); prefer another name.
- An exported host-language component needs a signature fence (F029) and a `runtime` (W117).

## Plain renderers

A plain renderer shows each component line as one literal line, container bodies as normal Markdown, leaf and inline fallbacks as text, definitions as code blocks, and `each` templates once. So: write fallbacks people can read, keep real content in container bodies rather than params, and keep a blank line around component lines so lists and paragraphs don't merge.

Base syntax is CommonMark + GFM (tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes, autolinks), alerts (`> [!NOTE]`), math (`$x$`, `$$…$$`, ```` ```math ````) and, opted in, wiki links. Raw HTML is sanitized; prefer Markdown and components. For a literal dollar amount next to another `$`, put a space or punctuation after the closing one, or escape it: `\$5`.

## Habits from other formats

| You might write | Write instead |
| --- | --- |
| `<Card title="Setup">…</Card>` (MDX/JSX) | `::: card {title="Setup"}` … `::: /card` |
| `<Chart data={sales} />` | `:: chart[Sales by month] {rows=(md.data.sales)}` |
| `{frontmatter.title}`, `{title}` (MDX) | `{{md.doc.title}}` |
| `{% callout type="tip" %}…{% /callout %}` (Markdoc) | `::: callout {kind=tip}` … `::: /callout` |
| `{% $user.name %}`, `{% if $x %}` (Markdoc) | `{{md.doc.user.name}}`, `::: if {when=(md.doc.x)}` |
| `::card{title="x"}` … `::` (MDC, remark-directive) | `::: card {title="x"}` … `::: /card` |
| `:::card` or a bare `:::` closer | `::: card` and `::: /card` |
| `#footer` or `<template #footer>` slot (MDC/Vue) | `:: #footer` on its own line |
| `::: {.note}`, `:::: columns` (Pandoc, Quarto) | `::: box {.note}` … `::: /box`; `::: row` … `::: /row` |
| `{{#each items}}…{{/each}}`, `{% for x in xs %}` | `::: each {in=(md.doc.items) as=item}` … `::: /each` |
| `{{ price * 2 }}`, `{{ name \| upcase }}` | `:value[$24]{of=(md.currency(md.doc.price * 2, "USD"))}`, `:value[NAME]{of=(md.doc.name.upperAscii())}` |
| `{{ items[0].name }}` | `:value[first]{of=(md.doc.items[0].name)}` |
| `$doc.title`, `${title}`, `page.title`, `site.data` | `{{md.doc.title}}`, `md.data.<as>` |
| `:badge[x] {a=b}` (space) | `:badge[x]{a=b}` |
| `items.length`, `a === b`, `x.includes(y)` | `size(items)`, `a == b`, `y in xs` (a list), `s.contains(t)` (a string) |
| `xs.sort((a, b) => a.n - b.n)` | `md.sortBy(xs, "n")` |
| `` `Total: ${n}` ``, `"n=" + n` | `"Total: " + string(n)` |
| `n.toFixed(2)`, `new Date()` | `md.number(n, 2)`, `md.today()` |
| `style="color: red"`, `margin`, `left`, `className` | closed params: `background`, `padding`, `inset-inline-start`, `.class` |
| a table row per item inside `each` | a table component: `:: table[Plans] {rows=(md.doc.plans)}` |
| `import Card from "./card"` in the body | `md: import:` in the frontmatter |
| wrapping a definition's body in `::: box {…}` | params on the definition fence |

## Diagnostics and their fixes

F codes are errors, W codes warnings. Each line: what it means → how to fix it.

- F001 major version not supported → `md: version: 1`.
- F002 unknown component → define it, import it, or fix the name; don't invent components the document has no definition or import for.
- F003 closer names the wrong container → close the innermost open one first; check the spelling.
- F004 container never closed → add `::: /name`.
- F005 closer with nothing open → remove it, or add the opener.
- F006 slot the component doesn't declare → use a declared slot name, or put the content in the default slot.
- F007 named slot given twice → merge the two into one `:: #name` section.
- F008 unknown param, or a breakpoint it doesn't take → use a declared param or a common param; `grid-area`, `scroll`, `fill`, `show`, `hide` and host-component params take no breakpoint; breakpoints are only `sm`, `md`, `lg`.
- F009 value doesn't fit the type → match the declared type, enum members or CSS grammar (tokens, logical lengths).
- F010 required param missing → give it.
- F011 broken param list → close quotes and brackets; quote values with spaces or parentheses; no `title=` without a value.
- F012 `::: +` not after an opener, leaf or continuation → move it directly under that line.
- F013 name clash or reserved name → rename: no `if`, `each`, `value`, `box`, `md`, no CEL reserved words or type names as definition params, `as` names or inputs, no two names differing only in `-` vs `_`.
- F014 unknown `{{path}}` → use `md.doc.`, `md.data.`, `md.input.` or a declared name; write `\{{` for literal braces.
- F015 slot line outside a container → move it inside, or remove it.
- F016 malformed component line → exactly `::: name`, `::: /name`, `::: + …`, `:: name[…]`, `:: #name`, with a space after the colons; no scoped names in the body.
- F017 param repeated, or `id` with `#name` → keep one.
- F018 body given to a component without slots → make it a leaf, or move the body out.
- F019 recursive definition → break the cycle.
- F020 import cycle → remove one import.
- F021 imported name not exported → check the source's exports and spelling.
- F022 `export.pack`/`version` differ from `package.json` → make them match.
- F023 name ambiguous between wildcard sources → list it explicitly under one import's `names`.
- F024 expression error, or a list or map interpolated → fix the CEL (types, `string()` for concatenation, `size()`, ints vs doubles); use `each` or `md.list` for lists.
- F025 an `each` iteration doesn't fit its `join` → `join=list`: only list items; `join=inline`: exactly one paragraph.
- F026 data or import source missing or bad → fix the path or package; relative paths stay inside the project; CSV headers must be unique and non-empty.
- F027 record doesn't fit its schema → fix the data, or make the field optional (`number?`) or a `string`.
- F028 remote origin not allowed → the processor's configuration decides; add a `fallback` file.
- F029 exported host component without a signature fence → add ```` ```compmd component=<name> signature ````.
- F030 `bind` or `input<…>` param names an undeclared input or one of another type → declare the input under `md: inputs:` with a matching type.
- F031 `from` interpolates something not allowed → only `md.input` and `md.doc`, never in a URL's scheme or host, never an input a host component can change.
- F032 closer for a container opened outside its list item or quote → open and close in the same item or quote.
- F033 frontmatter not plain YAML 1.2 → remove anchors, aliases, tags and duplicate keys.
- F034 expansion too large → filter or slice the data (`md.slice`), or nest fewer `each` blocks.
- F035 pack doesn't match its `integrity` → update the hash or the version.
- F036 param list on a signature fence → remove it; box params go on the definition fence.
- W101 leaf without fallback → add `[readable text]`.
- W102 language or runtime not supported → expect the fallback; write a good one.
- W103 `each` with one list item per iteration and no `join` → add `join=list`.
- W104 signature fence and component disagree → align the props and the signature.
- W105 local host component with untyped params → add a signature fence.
- W106 `{{` with something that isn't a path → use a path, `:value`, or `\{{`.
- W107 space before an inline component's `{` → remove the space.
- W108 component line right after a paragraph line → add a blank line before it.
- W109 interpolated URL with an unsafe scheme → use `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:` or a relative URL.
- W110 newer minor version than the processor → fine; features it lacks report their own errors.
- W111 unknown key under `md` → fix its spelling; author keys go outside `md`.
- W112 local name shadows a `@compmd/core` component → rename unless intended.
- W113 name from an ambient pack or `host:` data used → fine in that processor; not portable.
- W114 box whose blocks use breakpoints, sized by its content (in a `row`, not stretched in a `stack`, with `justify-self` in a `grid`, or positioned), and no `width` → give it a `width`.
- W115 host metadata ignored because the text has frontmatter → keep metadata in one place.
- W116 `::` line inside an HTML block → put a blank line after the HTML tag, or drop the HTML.
- W117 exported host component without `runtime` → add `runtime=react@19` (or `svelte@5`).
- W118 host component threw → fix the component; the fallback was shown.
- W119 box placing blocks by position has no height → give it `height`, `aspect-ratio` or `fill`.
- W120 box param given to a `display=contents` component → remove it; that component has no box.
